claims: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET (5:07 p.m. PT).
The Orion capsule landed after a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II mission returned from a journey around the moon.
The Artemis II crew was retrieved by the U.S. Navy and NASA personnel.
The Artemis II crew was flown to the USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II mission concluded with a fiery reentry and parachute-assisted landing.
According to the USAToday splashdown timeline, the crew module separated from the service module at 7:33 p.m. ET.
According to the USAToday splashdown timeline, the crew module initiated reentry at 7:53 p.m. ET.
According to the USAToday splashdown timeline, the crew module deployed parachutes just before 8:04 p.m. ET.
